{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Commerce One agreement — 18 rules assessed

## Executive summary

We reviewed the agreement against 18 playbook rules. Ten clauses are compliant (several at the fallback rather than the preferred position), six are deviations requiring redlines, and two rules have no usable clause at all.

The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitment, non-solicit or liquidated-damages obligation binding Corio; the vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is one-way in our favour and expressly carved out of the liability cap; the audit right is narrow and vendor-funded; renewals are one-year with a 30-day exit; and California law with San Francisco AAA arbitration sits within our accepted fallback list.

The risk is concentrated in four places. First, Section 13.5 flips ownership of Developments Corio creates to Commerce One wherever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an assignment of our IP to the vendor. Second, the Section 9 cap is measured by amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" and carries no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Third, Section 11 commits us to a five-year term with no convenience exit. Fourth, there is no vendor insurance covenant and no post-termination transition or data-return obligation in a hosted arrangement. Licence scope (Corio only, no affiliates or contractors) and the 60-day warranty that expires at or before acceptance are the remaining redlines.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 Indemnification | One-way vendor IP indemnity, uncapped via the Section 9 carve-out; exceeds fallback on the cap point. Scope is IP-only. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13.5 Shared Resources | "Unless" carve-out transfers Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; fails the fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Cap tied to a single transaction's fees; only carve-out is Section 8. Fails fallback on both cap basis and carve-outs. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.1 Miscellaneous | Mutual with an M&A carve-out, but consent is unfettered and there is no affiliate carve-out. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of Rights | Perpetual and irrevocable, but licences run to "Corio" only; no affiliates or contractors, and § 2.7 bars other access. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year term with automatic renewals; § 11.2 triggers limited to uncured breach and insolvency. No convenience exit for us. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 Grant of Rights | All licences non-exclusive; no sole-supplier covenant. Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 Grant of Rights | § 2.7 is licence-scope only; § 13.6 preserves independent development. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No penalty, late interest, shortfall or exit fee payable by Corio. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer | Remedy structure is fine, but the 60-day / 31 Dec 1999 window expires at or before acceptance testing; no services warranty. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 Term and Termination | § 11.3 covers Confidential Information only; no data return, format, timing or deletion obligation in a hosted model. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4.4 Fees | Once yearly, independent CPA acceptable to us, vendor-funded below a 5% threshold, records only. Notice is "reasonable" rather than fixed. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 14.3 Miscellaneous | California law, AAA in San Francisco. Within the fallback list; we prefer New York courts. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 4 Fees | No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation anywhere. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 4 Fees | Fees track licences granted, services provided and revenue actually invoiced; no take-or-pay. |
| 16 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binding Corio. |
| 17 | Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 11.1 Term and Termination | One-year renewals with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice. No reminder obligation and no uplift cap (and no uplift right). |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous | No insurance covenant at all, despite on-site personnel (§§ 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and vendor-operated MarketSite.net. |

## Walk-away items

Four findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 13.5 — vendor ownership of our Developments.** The support-linked carve-out assigns Customer IP to the vendor with no licence back. Smallest fix is deletion of the carve-out; if Commerce One needs rights in Developments it maintains, a licence from Corio is the sensible landing zone.
2. **§ 9 — per-transaction liability cap and absent carve-outs.** The cap must move to an aggregate 12 months' fees paid or payable (we have proposed the greater of that and US$1,000,000) with carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The US$1,000,000 floor can be dropped if the carve-outs are accepted.
3. **§ 11 — no customer termination for convenience across a five-year term.** We have proposed a new § 11.3 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit; 60–90 days is the fallback.
4. **§ 14 — no vendor insurance.** Commerce One touches our data and our premises. We have proposed a new § 14.10 at the preferred limits (CGL US$1M/2M, E&O US$2M, cyber US$5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), with fallback limits (E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M) available.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redlines on the six deviations and two missing rules: § 13.5 (delete ownership carve-out), § 9 (cap basis and carve-outs), § 14.1 (affiliate carve-out plus reasonableness standard), § 2 (extend licences to affiliates and contractors, with Corio responsible for compliance), § 11.3 (convenience right), § 11.4 (transition assistance and data return), § 7 (12-month warranty from acceptance, removing the 31 December 1999 cut-off, plus a professional and workmanlike services warranty), and § 14.10 (insurance, renumbering the existing § 14.10).
2. Confirm with the business the value of the affected transactions so we can defend the aggregate cap basis and the US$1,000,000 floor.
3. Identify which Developments Corio expects to create and which Commerce One would support on an ongoing basis, to scope the § 13.5 negotiation and any licence-back.
4. Note for the record, without redlining: the Section 8 indemnity is IP-only with a pro-rated refund; there is no renewal reminder or renewal price-increase cap; § 4.4 audit notice is "reasonable" rather than fixed and the auditor is not expressly bound by confidentiality; and the disclaimer text appears truncated in this copy — we should confirm the full text before signature.
5. Flag that ownership of enhancements to the Software itself is left to future negotiation in the final sentence of § 13.5; the business should decide whether to press that now."}
